subject: Novum canary: temporary SLO safety-net request and ramp plan
messages:
From: Eva Morales <eva@novum.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novum AI Legal <legal@novum.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary SLO safety-net for Novum canary

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput on the transformer variant looks promising. As we discussed, Novum intends to run an 8-week canary (alpha) of our recommendation product that will exercise the model under real traffic patterns. Based on our internal risk/ops, we need a short-term, explicit exception to Redwood's standard SLA for the canary window. High-level asks: 

- Duration: 8 weeks of canary traffic starting Dec 1, 2026, with an initial 2-week ramp.
- Latency: allow median latency up to 450ms for the canary model during the 2-week ramp (we anticipate median ~380ms after warm-up).
- Availability: accept a provisional uptime target of 95% for the canary variant during the ramp phase; full SLA to resume after ramp.
- Routing/fallback: we will route 20% of traffic to the canary initially; Redwood fallback to a stable model is required on error spikes.

Attached is our experiment plan and a redlined SLA template (novum_experiment_plan.pdf, sla-template.docx). Can you outline Redwood's requirements for granting this carveout (operational controls, monitoring hooks, rollback criteria, and requested signoffs)?

CCing Legal as they requested visibility. Quick note on timing: Novum's procurement team needs a signed carveout by Nov 28 to hit their internal launch calendar. If we can expedite review, that would be huge.

Best,
Eva Morales
Head of Product, Novum AI
mailto:eva@novum.ai

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Morales <eva@novum.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO safety-net for Novum canary

Eva — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. We can support a controlled carveout but will need to formalize operational guardrails. Outlining what we need from Novum and what Redwood will provide: 

What Redwood requires from Novum:
- Finalized experiment plan (you have a draft; please add explicit rollback thresholds and runbook contacts).
- A single point of contact for 24/7 on-call during the 2-week ramp (name and phone).
- Agreement to use our canary routing policy (start at 10-20%, escalate by monitored steps).

What Redwood will provide/commit to for the carveout window:
- Temporary SLO: median latency allowance up to 450ms during ramp window (as a written exception).
- Fallback: automatic routing to your pinned stable model on sustained error rate above 3% or latency p95 spike beyond 800ms.
- Observability: dedicated dashboard, token-level latency/throughput breakdown, and a daily incident digest.
- Rollback: we will auto-safeguard by throttling canary traffic if metrics cross agreed thresholds.

Operational timeline we propose:
- Internal technical review (Redwood infra + SRE): 3 business days.
- Legal review of carveout terms: 4 business days.
- Final signoff and DocuSign routing: by Nov 27 if we get materials today.

Karthik and Lauren: looping you both in — Karthik, can you confirm commercial considerations (credits/dedicated capacity asks)? Lauren, can you own the runbook/monitoring checklist with Novum?

Attached is a short draft of the proposed carveout terms (proposed-carveout-terms.pdf). If Novum can confirm the on-call contact and push a finalized experiment plan, we can target Nov 27 for signoff.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novum canary: commercial note

Quick commercial note — Novum indicated they may need some committed burst capacity during peak hours. For the carveout to not degrade gross margin, I'd propose: 

- 10% one-time usage credit applied to the first two months of canary usage (to offset tuning costs).
- If they want reserved capacity during the full 8 weeks, we scope a short-term Dedicated pool at a reduced rate (TBD).

I'll prepare a brief deal summary and escalate if Legal needs pricing specifics. Attaching a high-level deal_summary.xlsx.

Karthik
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Eva Morales <eva@novum.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novum AI Legal <legal@novum.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO safety-net for Novum canary

Laura / team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Novum accepts the proposed guardrails and will: 

- Share a finalized experiment plan with rollbacks and the on-call contact (Daniel Park, +1 (917) 555-3321) by EOD Nov 22.
- Start canary routing at 10% per your suggestion and abide by the auto-throttling thresholds.
- Accept the 10% one-time usage credit applied as you suggested; procurement will confirm pricing for any reserved pool if needed.

We are comfortable with the Nov 27 signoff timeline and will prioritize the doc changes. Please send over the DocuSign when ready.
